item.title: September 25, 2026
item.description: I came across this post from Amit Sahai. The most important point he makes is to invest into the collective human understanding of new ideas discovered by AI or a human-AI collaboration. It’ll be a waste if we fail to use the new results to develop a deeper understanding of the world. And it’ll very bad, perhaps even lethal, to live in a world surrounded by systems that no human understands.

item.title: September 20, 2026
item.description:
KK’s essay is enlightning. His description that capabilities of LLMs is an emergent property of tranformation of millions of sources into the latent space is sharp.

I also find the comment ’the latent space is the new commons’ interesting. Needless to say, LLMs are incredibly powerful. It’s strategically important to saturate LLMs, both for a nation that wants to remain relevant and humanity to progress at a rapid pace. And it’s a shame that the frontier models are not universally available (even when one is willing to pay the cost). I hope governments recognize this and direct substantial portion of tax payer’s money to (a) develop public intelligence, and (b) have LLMs saturate in its population.

item.title: September 14, 2026
item.description: This article from pocoo is closely related to some of our product thinking on PAC. It’s true that LLMs are incredibly useful in pursuing ‘random’ interests, or long-due ideas/experiments, not only for hackers but, increasingly, for the general crowd. Many of the interests are nothing new. It’s likely that someone has already tried out something similar before. And so, a LLM gradually nudges the user towards a suitable solution. A unsurprising consequence of this is that the end results often overlap.

item.title: Yet another privacy solution on Ethereum
item.description: There are multiple approaches for privacy on public blockchains: 2-state commitment+nullifier model, MPC/threshold-FHE, and TEEs. Each with its own set of benefits & limitations. Here I attempt to sketch yet another privacy solution. Like others, it has limitations and some advantages. It’s limited in the sense that it does not provide as strong as privacy guarantees as 2-state commitment+nullifer model. Its advantages are that it’s compatible with the EVM state model, while providing stronger guarantees than any FHE/MPC solution, or validiums.
